question.:question/problem: If the path $C$ is the line segment $\overline{AB}$ traversed from the point $A(0,3)$ to the point $B(1,-1),$ then ${\int }_C \left(2 x\right)\,dx+\left(- 2 x y\right)\,dy=$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=3\,j$ and $b=i-j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\   & =3\,j+t\left(i-j-\left(3\,j\right)\right) \\   & =3\,j+t\left(i-4\,j\right) \\   & =\left(t\right)\,i+\left(3 - 4 t\right)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=t$ and $y(t)=3 - 4 t$ along the segment.

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=i-4\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C \left(2 x\right)\,dx+\left(- 2 x y\right)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(2 x\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 2 x y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(\left(2 x\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 2 x y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(2\right)\cdot \left(t\right)\cdot \left(1\right)+\left(-2\right)\cdot \left(t\right)\cdot \left(3 - 4 t\right)\cdot \left(-4\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(2 t\right)+\left(- 32 t^{2} + 24 t\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}- 32 t^{2} + 26 t\,dt \\   & =\left[- \frac{32 t^{3}}{3} + 13 t^{2}\right]_0^1 \\   & =\left(- \frac{32 \left(1\right)^{3}}{3} + 13 \left(1\right)^{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{32 \left(0\right)^{3}}{3} + 13 \left(0\right)^{2}\right) \\   & =\left(\left(- \frac{32}{3}\right)+\left(13\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If the path $C$ is the line segment $\overline{AB}$ traversed from the point $A(2,-4)$ to the point $B(3,0),$ then ${\int }_C \left(3 x\right)\,dx+\left(- 2 y\right)\,dy=$

The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=2\,i-4\,j$ and $b=3\,i.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\   & =2\,i-4\,j+t\left(3\,i-\left(2\,i-4\,j\right)\right) \\   & =2\,i-4\,j+t\left(i+4\,j\right) \\   & =\left(t + 2\right)\,i+\left(4 t - 4\right)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=t + 2$ and $y(t)=4 t - 4$ along the segment.

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=i+4\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C \left(3 x\right)\,dx+\left(- 2 y\right)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(3 x\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 2 y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(\left(3 x\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 2 y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(3\right)\cdot \left(t + 2\right)\cdot \left(1\right)+\left(-2\right)\cdot \left(4 t - 4\right)\cdot \left(4\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(3 t + 6\right)+\left(32 - 32 t\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}38 - 29 t\,dt \\   & =\left[- \frac{29 t^{2}}{2} + 38 t\right]_0^1 \\   & =\left(- \frac{29 \left(1\right)^{2}}{2} + 38 \left(1\right)\right)-\left(- \frac{29 \left(0\right)^{2}}{2} + 38 \left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\left(\left(- \frac{29}{2}\right)+\left(38\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\frac{47}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=-3\,i-3\,j$ and $b=i-2\,j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\   & =-3\,i-3\,j+t\left(i-2\,j-\left(-3\,i-3\,j\right)\right) \\   & =-3\,i-3\,j+t\left(4\,i+j\right) \\   & =\left(4 t - 3\right)\,i+\left(t - 3\right)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x(t)=4 t - 3$ and $y(t)=t - 3$ along the segment.

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=4\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C \left(3 x\right)\,dx+\left(3 y\right)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(3 x\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(3 y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(\left(3 x\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(3 y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(3\right)\cdot \left(4 t - 3\right)\cdot \left(4\right)+\left(3\right)\cdot \left(t - 3\right)\cdot \left(1\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(48 t - 36\right)+\left(3 t - 9\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}51 t - 45\,dt \\   & =\left[\frac{51 t^{2}}{2} - 45 t\right]_0^1 \\   & =\left(\frac{51 \left(1\right)^{2}}{2} - 45 \left(1\right)\right)-\left(\frac{51 \left(0\right)^{2}}{2} - 45 \left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\left(\left(\frac{51}{2}\right)+\left(-45\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right) \\   & =- \frac{39}{2}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\   & =-4\,i-3\,j+t\left(-2\,i-4\,j-\left(-4\,i-3\,j\right)\right) \\   & =-4\,i-3\,j+t\left(2\,i-j\right) \\   & =\left(2 t - 4\right)\,i+\left(- t - 3\right)\,j,\end{aligned}

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=2\,i-j.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_C \left(- x\right)\,dx+\left(- 3 y\right)\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(- x\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 3 y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(\left(- x\right)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\left(- 3 y\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(-1\right)\cdot \left(2 t - 4\right)\cdot \left(2\right)+\left(-3\right)\cdot \left(- t - 3\right)\cdot \left(-1\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\left(8 - 4 t\right)+\left(- 3 t - 9\right)\,dt \\   & ={\int }_{0}^{1}- 7 t - 1\,dt \\   & =\left[- \frac{7 t^{2}}{2} - t\right]_0^1 \\   & =\left(- \frac{7 \left(1\right)^{2}}{2} - \left(1\right)\right)-\left(- \frac{7 \left(0\right)^{2}}{2} - \left(0\right)\right) \\   & =\left(\left(- \frac{7}{2}\right)+\left(-1\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)+\left(0\right)\right) \\   & =- \frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}

$$
